title: Graceful degradation for rerank service: adaptive timeouts, circuit breakers, and regional failover
creator: Priya N. Rao
description: Implement an integrated strategy for reranking endpoint resilience that balances quality (embeddings+rerank), tail latency, and scale. Work includes adaptive per-request timeouts, per-backend circuit breakers, prioritized fallback routing to cheaper/geo-local model variants, and a lightweight graceful-degradation mode that returns cached or approximate scores when strict ranking cannot be met within SLOs. Goal: reduce P99 latency spikes, prevent cascading failures across regions, and preserve user-visible quality with measurable SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for rerank endpoint decreases by >= 30% on bursty traffic compared to baseline during load tests
When upstream model pool in a region crosses failure threshold, traffic is automatically routed to configured fallback region or model variant within 5s
At least 95% of requests receive a ranked response; remaining requests receive deterministic graceful-degradation output (cached or quick heuristic) documented in API changelog
Circuit breaker metrics (open/close events) emitted to observability and surfaced in Console per-route dashboard
Automated chaos test (simulated high-latency per-node) passes without higher-level service outage and without data loss
design_decisions: Use leaky-bucket adaptive timeout algorithm: per-route baseline + percentile-based headroom from rolling window of latencies
Circuit breakers are token-bucket based per-backend (model instance pool) with soft-fail (return heuristic) and hard-fail (route to fallback region) states
Fallback hierarchy: 1) same-region cached VK/heuristic score, 2) same-region cheaper quantized model, 3) adjacent-region compatible model, 4) global best-effort model
Prefer routing policy that respects customer config: customers can pin region/model variants; pinning prevents automatic cross-region fallback unless customer opts-in
Expose toggles via Console and API: graceful_degradation=true/false, max_cross_region_failover per-route, and circuit_breaker thresholds
implementation_notes: Add new reranker middleware layer to enforce per-request deadline and observe actual tail latencies
Instrument model-serving pool to report success/latency/failure histograms and expose token-bucket state via runtime API
Integrate routing policy into Smart Router with priority list evaluation and atomic fallback steps to avoid split-brain
Caching: implement prefix cache for rerank inputs with TTL; cache keys include embedding fingerprint + query hash
Store fallback policies in existing customer config store; ensure migration path for legacy configs
Backwards compatible API: default behavior unchanged for all customers; new behaviors require opt-in via route config during pilot
testing_plan: Unit tests for timeout/leaky-bucket math, breaker state transitions, and routing decision tree
Integration tests with local mock model servers to simulate slow/failed nodes and verify fallback path ordering
Load tests: reproduce burst patterns (traffic spikes, cold-cache spikes) and measure P50/P95/P99 before/after
Chaos testing: randomly delay and drop 20% of model backend responses across regions; assert graceful-degradation output rate and SLOs
A/B rollout in staging then canary in production for small set of tenants with observability dashboards monitored
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy middleware + metrics in staging; run synthetic workload and iterate on timeout heuristics
Week 2: Enable canary for internal teams and 3 low-risk customers; monitor circuit breaker events and false-positive rates
Week 3: Expand to 20% of production traffic with automated rollback triggers based on increased error rate or quality regressions
Week 4: Full rollout with post-launch review; provide opt-out path for customers who require strict single-region execution
Emergency rollback: feature-flag off at Smart Router and middleware layer; documented runbook in Ops Channel
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards: per-route rerank latency percentiles, breaker state counts, fallback-routing events, and graceful-degradation ratio
Alerts: >5 open breakers for a region for 1m, graceful-degradation ratio >5% sustained for 5m, cross-region failover rate spike >10%
SLOs: 99th percentile latency target for rerank endpoint with burst allowance documented; error budget burn rate tracked
Logging: structured events for each fallback decision with request_id, cause (timeout/failure), and chosen fallback node/model
